candidates.title: Will the maximum temperature be 68-69° on Nov 20, 2026?
candidates.rules_primary: If the maximum temperature recorded at Chicago (CLIMDW) for Nov 20, 2026, is between 68-69° fahrenheit according to The Weather Company, then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary:
Not all weather data is the same. While checking a source like AccuWeather or Google Weather may help guide your decision, the official and final value used to determine this market is the maximum/minimum temperature as reported by the Weather Company.

Reading weather data
Preliminary Weather Company data may be subject to rounding and conversion differences from the final reported value.
Use caution when interpreting preliminary Weather Company readings.

If it is determined in the sole discretion of the Exchange that there is a material error in the initial non-preliminary publication, Expiration may be held until the publication of a non-materially-erroneous data revision or until the Expiration Date, whichever comes first. If no data is available at the end of this period, all markets will resolve to the last fair price determined by Kalshi. Please note, a status of "Final" on weather.com/kalshi is provided for convenience only, and does not guarantee data to be error-free and thus exempt from the above.

candidates.title: Will CPI Core rise more than 0.3% in November?
candidates.rules_primary: If the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy for November 2026, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, increases by above 0.3%, then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary:
Please note that the value of the Underlying is the single-decimal value reported by the BLS.

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

candidates.title: Will there be at least 40 presidential nominations sent to the Senate in the week of Nov 15, 2026?
candidates.rules_primary: If Donald Trump has sent at least 40 nominations to the U.S. Senate from Nov 15, 2026 through Nov 21, 2026 (as checked on the “Presidential Actions” page at whitehouse.gov before 10:00 AM ET on Nov 22, 2026), then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved

The market solely resolves to the publication dates visibly displayed on the "Presidential Actions" tab at whitehouse.gov before 10:00 AM ET on Nov 22, 2026.
The week runs from Nov 15, 2026 through Nov 21, 2026.

Payout criteria

If a person receives multiple qualifying nominations within the period, they will each count separately.
For example, Trump's March 4 nomination of Kevin Warsh is considered two nominations.

candidates.title: Will the Democratic party win the Senate in 2028?
candidates.rules_primary: If the Democratic party has won control of the Senate in 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary: This market may be determined early based on a consensus of media calls projecting control of the U.S. Senate. See full rules for details. Otherwise, victory will be determined by the party identification of the President pro tempore of the Senate on February 1, 2029.

candidates.title: Will the “This Week” weighted average advertised price for Avocados, Hass, each, for November 20, 2026 be above $1.00?
candidates.rules_primary: If the “This Week” weighted average advertised price for Avocados, Hass, each, as reported in the USDA AMS Weekly Grocery Store Specialty Crops Feature Activity report scheduled for publication on November 20, 2026 is above $1.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary: This market uses advertised retail prices, not transaction prices. The relevant value is the “This Week” Wtd Avg Price for the row with Commodity “Avocados,” Variety “Hass,” and Unit “each” in the National Conventional Summary section of the USDA AMS Weekly Grocery Store Specialty Crops Feature Activity report. Prices for other avocado varieties, sizes, package counts, organic avocados, regional tables, “Last Week,” or “Last Year” do not count.

candidates.title: Will core CPI inflation MoM exceed headline CPI inflation MoM for November 2026?
candidates.rules_primary: If core CPI inflation MoM is above headline CPI inflation MoM for November 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary:
Only the first non-preliminary release of each value will be used. Revisions published after the first non-preliminary release will not affect resolution.

For purposes of this market, “core CPI” means the seasonally adjusted one-month percent change for “All items less food and energy” in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, as reported by BLS. “Headline CPI” means the seasonally adjusted one-month percent change for “All items” in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, as reported by BLS. The comparison will use the one-decimal values reported by BLS. If the values are equal, the market resolves No.

candidates.title: Will a bill ending self rule in Washington DC become law before Jan 1, 2027?
candidates.yes_sub_title: A bill ending self rule in Washington DC
candidates.rules_primary: If a bill ending self rule in Washington DC becomes law before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.

candidates.title: Will Trump nominate Kevin Hassett as a member of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System before Jan 1, 2027?
candidates.rules_primary: If Kevin Hassett is nominated as a member of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027. then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary: Official announcements made by the President (or President-elect) of Kevin Hassett's nomination shall satisfy the Payout Criterion, even if they are not yet sent to the Senate.

candidates.title: Will seasonally adjusted month-over-month percentage change in core goods CPI for November 2026 be above -0.2%?
candidates.rules_primary: If the seasonally adjusted month-over-month percentage change in core goods CPI for November 2026 is above -0.2%, then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary:
“Core goods CPI” means “Commodities less food and energy commodities” in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. city average, as published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Resolution uses the seasonally adjusted month-over-month percent change for November 2026 published in the first BLS CPI release reporting that month’s data, at its published precision. The value will not be recalculated from index levels. Subsequent revisions, including revisions to seasonal adjustments, will not affect resolution.

candidates.title: Will the 12-month percentage change in CPI-U in December 2028 be above 0.0%?
candidates.rules_primary: If the 12-month percentage change in CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted, in December 2028 is above 0.0%, then the market resolves to Yes.
candidates.rules_secondary: The initially reported value for December 2028 will be used. This market concerns the 12-month percentage change for December 2028, not the annual-average percentage change for the specified year.
